text:
maria: FYI noticed a big spike in 503s and backend CPU right after the tokenizer push at 12:04Z. Prefix cache hit-rate dropped from ~78% -> ~9% in 3m. Traffic to model-x soaked the origin.
ops-bot: deploy user/maria/tokenizer-update succeeded at 2026-03-15T12:04:08Z

sam: digging in. quick numbers: total requests 24k/min, cache lookups 22k/min, hits 2k/min. Miss amplification: many identical prompts that used to hit are now unique keys.

lee: is this a cache keying change? we didn't touch cache code in that deploy AFAIK.

sam: right — we didn't change KV cache. The tokenizer change altered tokenization normalization (collapsed repeated spaces into single tokens + changed token boundaries). Cache keying uses token-derived prefix for some models. so same human prompt -> different token sequence -> new key.

sam: profiler dump (condensed):
```
kv_cache: lookups=22012 hits=2018 miss=19994 hit_rate=0.091
backend: avg_latency=480ms p95=1.2s cpu=85%
hotset: top-100 before: 82% traffic, top-100 now: 18% -> hotset evaporated
```

sam: old key function (simplified):
```
def cache_key(prompt):
    # pre-tokenizer path
    prefix = prompt[:1024]
    return sha256(prefix.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
```
new keying used tokens directly (introduced in tokenizer update):
```
def cache_key_from_tokens(tokens):
    # token-based prefixing
    return sha256(' '.join(tokens[:160]).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
```

maria: so identical visible prompts map to different keys now. that explains the miss surge.

lee: mitigation options: 1) rollback tokenizer, 2) disable prefix caching for model-x, 3) add a compatibility key-path that falls back to raw-text key. Which is fastest?

ops-bot: emergency action: prefix-cache disabled for model-x at 12:12 by @maria (route: /v1/generate model-x).

sre-oncall: confirm: traffic fell back to origin and latency increased but backend errors dropped after disable?

sam: after disable: cache lookups dropped by 92% (since we short-circuit), backend latency p50 rose from 120ms->210ms but 503s dropped to baseline. CPU dropped to 58%.

aisha: short term we should keep cache disabled and roll back tokenizer change to reestablish stable keying. medium-term: we need integration tests that assert cache key invariants across tokenizer changes and a warmup strategy (background priming).

lee: quick patch idea: implement dual-keying on lookup: attempt token-key -> raw-prefix-key -> origin. That would buy us compatibility without full rollback. overhead is one extra lookup on misses.

sam: implemented a quick dual-key lookup in staging, looks fine. but re-enabling in prod requires warmup; otherwise we'll re-create the miss storm.

maria: rolling back tokenizer update at 12:25.

ops-bot: rollback user/maria/tokenizer-update completed at 2026-03-15T12:25:40Z

sam: after rollback we ran a controlled re-enable of prefix cache at 12:40 with background priming script that walks recent top prompts and pre-populates keys. hit-rate climbed back to ~75% over 10m.

maria: resolution: root cause = tokenization-induced key-space divergence. immediate fix = rollback + background warmup.

aisha: action items: @sam add unit/integration tests that cover cache_key invariants + tokenization changes; @lee implement opt-in dual-key lookup w/ feature flag; @maria add deploy checklist step to run cache-compat check for any tokenizer/normalization change; @sre-oncall add alert: kv_cache.hit_rate drop below 50% for model-x for >2m triggers pager.

sre-oncall: filed incident PRD and postmortem. will schedule postmortem in incident channel tomorrow.

maria: thanks all — re-enable looks stable. leaving cache disabled on dev clusters until tests land. :thumbsup:
